ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: The many blind people feeling an elephant each encounter a part and mistake partial contact for the whole animal.
EvidenceBody: Xiangtian Jinian explicitly reads the elephant comparison as exposing the illness of clinging to one's own view. Dahui Zonggao lists it among cases that must be met personally rather than settled in speech. Xutang Zhiyu says the blind know an elephant yet do not see the whole; an unnamed questioner asks Zhaozhou what the true elephant is when each gives a different account, and Zhaozhou answers that there is no reliance—one simply does not know. The Chan bend turns the comparison into a public test of whether partial descriptions are being promoted as complete seeing.
